extracted.intended_audience: members of r/DestructiveReaders and writers seeking blunt, detailed peer critique
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting and providing high-effort, honest peer critiques on the r/DestructiveReaders subreddit, using a two-phase format (line edit + critique essay) and a 1:1 word-count effort requirement. Emphasizes deconstructive feedback focused on craft elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-Effort / 1:1 ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: All critiques must be high-effort and follow the 1:1 ratio — build a critique with the same word count or more than the story you submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Google Doc comments don't count toward the 1:1 ratio. Critics are expected to invest equal or greater writing effort than the original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Phase Critique Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques must have two phases: a line edit and a critique essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format separates micro-level issues from macro-level analysis so writers can see boundaries between skills and understand techniques used incorrectly and how they affect the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line edit
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 1: Focuses on style, grammar, dialogue, and confusing passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides line-by-line notes on wording, sentence-level problems, mechanical issues, and places that cause confusion for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique essay
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 2: Focuses individually on title, style, plot, character, and pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more holistic, essay-form analysis that diagnoses larger structural and craft issues and explains their effects on the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone — Unfiltered honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback is unfiltered and unapologetically honest; the community prioritizes reader honesty over cushioning feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect blunt, direct statements about what bothers readers and why; critiques may 'tear writing apart' if it isn't working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-by-line diagnostic approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques often include a line-by-line breakdown of what bothers the reader, what to improve, and what's missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This granular approach makes specific problems visible and actionable rather than vague or purely impressionistic commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on discrete craft categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The community treats craft elements (title, opening, voice, plot, character, pacing, etc.) as separable, diagnosable categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should identify which craft element is failing, explain how it fails, and suggest concrete fixes or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how well the title serves the piece (evokes interest, fits tone/theme, sets reader expectations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the critique essay phase; identify whether title helps or hinders the reader and suggest stronger alternatives if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the strength of the opening in grabbing attention and establishing stakes, voice, or conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should note whether the beginning creates momentum or stalls and recommend ways to tighten or reframe the opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style / voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the distinctness, consistency, and appropriateness of the narrative voice and stylistic choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out tonal inconsistencies, problematic stylistic tics, or places where voice elevates or undermines the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot structure and momentum
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the arrangement of events and whether the story maintains forward motion and logical cause-effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify structural holes, weak or extraneous scenes, pacing of revelations, and places where momentum lags or rushes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization (depth, distinctness, motivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess characters for depth, distinct voices, clear motivations, and believable development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out flat or interchangeable characters, unclear goals, or motivation that doesn't justify behavior; suggest ways to deepen or differentiate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the rhythm and tempo of the story—how scenes are balanced and whether the narrative feels rushed or sluggish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note sections that need tightening or expansion and how pacing choices affect tension and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the realism, distinctness, and functional purpose of dialogue in advancing character and plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight stilted, expository, or indistinguishable dialogue; suggest ways to make speech patterns unique and purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar / mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sentence-level correctness: grammar, punctuation, spelling, and other mechanical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed primarily in the line edit phase; indicate consistent errors vs. one-off slips and recommend fixes or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusing passages / clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out passages that confuse the reader and explain what is unclear and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether confusion comes from wording, logic, insufficient detail, or structural choices, and offer ways to clarify.
